pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of OLUMIANT for the treatment of severe alopecia areata have been established in pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. Use of OLUMIANT for this indication is supported by evidence from an adequate and well-controlled trial that included a total of 316 pediatric subjects 12 years of age and older weighing at least 30 kg who were exposed to OLUMIANT for at least one year. Overall, the safety profile observed in pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with severe alopecia areata treated with OLUMIANT is consistent with the safety profile in adults with severe alopecia areata [ see Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 ), Pharmacokinetics ( 12.3 ), Clinical Studies ( 14.3 )] . The safety and effectiveness of OLUMIANT for the treatment of severe alopecia areata have not been established in pediatric patients younger than 12 years of age. The safety and effectiveness of OLUMIANT for the treatment of juvenile idiopathic arthritis or COVID-19 have not been established in pediatric patients.

interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS In patients taking strong Organic Anion Transporter 3 (OAT3) inhibitors (e.g., probenecid), reduce the recommended OLUMIANT dosage. ( 2.7 , 7.1 ) 7.1 Strong OAT3 Inhibitors Baricitinib exposure is increased when OLUMIANT is co-administered with strong OAT3 inhibitors (such as probenecid), hence the dosage of baricitinib should be reduced by half the recommended dose [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.7 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . 7.2 Other JAK Inhibitors or Biologic DMARDs OLUMIANT has not been studied in combination with other JAK inhibitors or with biologic DMARDs [see Indications and Usage ( 1.1 , 1.2 , 1.3 )] .
